conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling emotionally now that your baby is here. We’ll be using a short, well-trusted set of questions called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It simply helps us see how common post-pregnancy mood and anxiety symptoms might be showing up for you.

Everything we talk about stays between us unless there’s an immediate safety concern, and you can answer honestly—there’s no judgment. It’s just 10 quick questions about the past seven days, and we’ll move at whatever pace feels comfortable for you. Ready to start?

First, looking back over the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? It’s been kind of hard. I still laugh sometimes when my husband or my sister says something silly, but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to—maybe once or twice in the past week. Most of the time I feel too tired to even notice humor.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah… I can still laugh a little, but it’s definitely not as often. Things that used to crack me up right away feel kind of flat lately.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but lately it feels like there’s nothing I’m truly looking forward to. I still do those things, but the “looking-forward” part is mostly gone; it feels more like I’m just getting through the day.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Like, if the baby won’t settle, I’ll catch myself thinking maybe I’m doing something wrong or not doing enough tummy time, even when everyone says he’s fine. It’s not every hour or anything, but a couple of times this week I’ve gone to bed replaying little moments and feeling guilty about stuff I probably couldn’t control.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah, that happens. I’ll be sitting on the couch, baby’s asleep in the bassinet, and suddenly my heart starts racing because I’m sure he’s too quiet—even though I can see his chest moving. It’s not constant, but it pops up a few times a day, and it’s hard to shake until I check on him one more time.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-blown panics, but once or twice this week I’ve had that sudden rush—like I’m bracing for something awful to happen, even though nothing’s going on. It passes pretty fast, maybe a minute or two, but it leaves me jittery for a while.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… I feel like I’m treading water most days. The diapers, feedings, trying to squeeze in a shower—if one extra thing pops up, like the dog needing to go out or a sink full of bottles, I get this tight-chest feeling that I can’t quite catch up.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

A few nights this week I’ve lain there wired after the baby’s finally down—my mind just keeps looping through little worries or things I “should” have done better. I wouldn’t say I’m miserable-miserable, but it’s enough restlessness that I’ve stared at the ceiling for an hour or two before drifting off.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad sometimes, yeah. It’s not every minute, but there have been a couple of evenings where I just sat on the couch with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It usually passes after a while, but it lingers longer than I’d like.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Not really. I got a little teary one night when the baby wouldn’t latch and I was running on three hours of sleep, but it didn’t turn into actual crying. So, no, no real crying spells this week.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. That hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit

Symptoms endorsed  
- Reduced ability to experience pleasure/enthusiasm (Q1, Q2)  
- Mild-moderate anhedonia and persistent low mood with “heavy, empty” feeling (Q8)  
- Sleep disturbance secondary to ruminating worries (Q7)  
- Frequent, excessive self-blame surrounding infant care (Q3)  
- Multiple daily episodes of unprovoked anxiety, brief surges of panic (Q4, Q5)  
- Sense of being overwhelmed and “treading water,” with physiological stress response (Q6)

Pattern  
Consistent with subsyndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms arising in postpartum period; functional impact present (difficulty sleeping, jittery, tight-chest, restlessness). No anhedonia-exclusion; mood lability noted.

Areas of screening significance  
- Postpartum depression (EPDS items 1, 2, 7, 8, 9) – mild range  
- Postpartum anxiety/panic spectrum (EPDS items 4, 5, 6) – moderate range  
- Coping/self-efficacy concerns (item 6)

Risk factors identified  
✓ Persistent sadness + loss of enjoyment  
✓ Sleep disruption linked to mood rumination  
✓ Guilt/self-criticism out of proportion to circumstances  
✓ Anxiety symptoms >50% of days with brief panic-equivalents  
✓ No self-harm ideation reported (Q10 negative) → no acute safety concern

Screening observation  
Patient exhibits clinically significant postpartum mood/anxiety symptoms that exceed “baby blues” threshold; impairment in enjoyment, sleep, and daily coping. Recommends formal EPDS scoring, collateral psychosocial review, and consideration of referral for perinatal mental health evaluation.
